tasks.title: ✦ decides by itself; Settings and Agents tabs; no 1·2·3 on Today
tasks.acceptance: ✦ has no kind buttons: Cortex decides (kept in Cortex, reminder, found, answer, proposal) and the result's colour shows which; no voice-system button; a tiny attach; shortcuts set under Systems › Settings (open ✦, start speaking unassigned, open the chat); Settings lists every setting with a link to where it lives; Today has no number-key approvals; Systems › Agents lists coding agents as switchable resources with order, state and a hand-over prompt.
tasks.validation: tests/test_screen.py, tests/test_agents.py; browser check

tasks.title: Builder falls back to the next ready coding agent when Claude is out
tasks.acceptance: When Claude's usage limit is reached, the dev loop runs the next ready agent from engine/agents.py (first Codex CLI, `codex exec`) on the same task with the hand-over prompt, logs which agent built it, and returns to Claude after the reset; nothing changes when no other agent is installed.
tasks.validation: tests with a mocked agent command; one real run on the Pi

tasks.title: One numbering in ✦ and the chat; quick exchanges saved only on request
tasks.acceptance: Choices and proposals share one numbering (choices first), so no number appears twice; no Yes/No row (click or press the number, Esc dismisses); a ✦ exchange is not written into the Cortex conversation unless the owner presses Continue in the chat, which saves it as a conversation.
tasks.validation: tests/test_screen.py; browser check

tasks.title: Cortex answer quality: per-job model and thinking, no forced brevity, sees matching tasks
tasks.acceptance: [models.jobs.<job>] in the constitution can set model, thinking_tokens, max_tokens and claude_code_model for one job (e.g. chat on Opus with thinking); Cortex is no longer told to be concise; besides the top 40 open tasks it sees tasks matching the conversation and the total count.
tasks.validation: tests/test_models_jobs.py

tasks.title: Cortex chat on Claude Code: streaming, real turns, web search, Atlas look-ups, files
tasks.acceptance: Without an API key, the Cortex chat streams its answer, keeps one Claude Code session per conversation, can search the web, looks things up in Atlas through a read-only MCP server, reads files attached to the conversation, finds earlier conversations, follows a full Cortex brief, and changes nothing except through numbered proposals; it falls back to the one-shot answer when Claude Code is unavailable.
tasks.validation: tests/test_cortex.py; browser check with a stand-in Claude Code
